ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper left node is A, the upper right node is B, and the lower common connection point is C. Between A and B there is a voltage source Us, with the left end marked “+” and the right end marked “-”. Between A and C there is a 1Ω resistor connected; between C and B there is a 3Ω resistor connected, and beside the 3Ω branch there is an upward 2A current marked. At the lower port there is an upward 1A current entering node C, and the upper right port is also marked with a 1A direction pointing toward the circuit. Reasoning: The current in the 3Ω resistor is 2A and the direction is from C to B, so V_C−V_B=2×3=6V. Write KCL for node C: the lower 1A enters C, and the 3Ω branch has 2A flowing from C toward B and leaving C, so another 1A is needed to flow from A into C through the 1Ω branch. Therefore across the 1Ω resistor, V_A−V_C=1×1=1V. Us is defined according to the polarity in the figure as V_A−V_B, so Us=(V_A−V_C)+(V_C−V_B)=1+6=7V.

method.method_draft: Let the left top node be A, the right top node be B, and the lower common node be C. From the image, the 3 Ω resistor carries 2 A upward, so V_C − V_B = 2×3 = 6 V. Apply KCL at node C: 1 A enters from the lower terminal and 2 A leaves upward through the 3 Ω branch, so the remaining 1 A must enter C through the 1 Ω branch from A to C. Thus V_A − V_C = 1×1 = 1 V. Since U_S is defined with + at A and − at B, U_S = V_A − V_B = (V_A − V_C) + (V_C − V_B) = 1 + 6 = 7 V.
